2. Short facts leading to this rule are that the plaintiff opposite parties instituted a Title Suit for declaration of title and confirmation of possession in the suit land. On the prayer Of the plaintiffs' and ad interim' order of injunction was issued by the tied "Munsif on 30.1.71 against the defendant petitioner restraining him from entering into the suit land, constructing any structure thereon or in any way disturbing the possession of the plaintiff in the suit land. On 9.2.71 the defendant petitioner appeared and filed written objection and on 10.2.71 on the prayer of the defendant petitioner, an Advocate Commissioner for local investigation was appointed or 18.9.71 the learned Munsif after hearing hot the parties passed the following order:- It is ordered that both the sides to maintain status quo till disposal of the suit Inform: 

 3. According to the allegations made by the plaintiff opposite parties; the defendant-petitioner isolates the order of 'status quo by entering into the suit land, cutting trees therefrom and excavating earth therein for construction of a hut. Upon these allegations, a Miscellaneous case was started which was contested by the defendant petitioner by filing a written objection. The plaintiffs and the defendant examined 3 witnesses each in support of their respective cases. Upon a consideration of the same the learned Munsif found the defendant guilty under Order 39 rule 2(3) of the Code of Civil Procedure and attached his property for 1 month and directed him to be detained in civil prison for 7 days. On appeal by the defendant, the learned Subordinate Judge affirmed the Order of the learned Munsif. Hence the present rule at the instance of the defendant. 

 4. It appears that on the prayer of the plaintiff the learned Munsif passed an ex parte order of ad interim injunction on 30-1-71 restraining the defendant-petitioner from entering into the suit land, making any construction thereon and from interfering in any manner with the possession of the plaintiff in the suit land. The order of ad interim injunction was contested by the defendant petitioner by filing a written objection and by this order dated 18-9-71 the Learned Munsif after hearing both the parties directed maintenance of status quo till the disposal of the suit. From a perusal of the orders dated 30-1-71 and 18-9-71. It appears that the learned Munsif was not satisfied about the claim of the plaintiff regarding his possession in the, suit land, and accordingly modified his earlier order of ad interim injunction to an order for maintenance of status quo. If the learned Munsif was prima facie satisfied about the plaintiff's claim of possession in the suit land there was no reason for him not to make the ad interim order absolute. But instead of doing so he modified his earlier order of status. Now status quo means the existing state of things at any given time. The position, therefore, boils down to this, that by the order of status quo the parties were directed to maintain their respective positions without interfering with each other. Before anyone can be punished for disobedience of an order status quo, it is the duty of the Court to corner to a positive finding regarding the possession of the other party in the suit land: Unfortunately; neither of the courts below appears to have considered the question in its proper perspective nor have they come to any finding regarding the possession of the plaintiff is the suit land where the alleged violation took place. On the Contrary, it transpires froth the evidence on record that the 'suit' land is in possession of opposite party No. 2; (defendant No. 22) who had constructed  house on the  suit land after obtaining necessary permission from the Municipality and had also asserted his possession in the suit land inlays evidence before the Court. This assertion by the petitioner was not challenged by the opposite party in their counter affidavit. I am therefore of the opinion that the impugned order cannot be sustained in law.
